title: Explaining The Situation
paragraphs: If we let the pig escape, nothing good will come of it, and taking down Trash would make things easier in the long run.
“Éclair is being held?”

“She’s a noble’s daughter who advocates for demi-human rights. That’s what future Father and the female knight call her. I was told to remember her name properly, but… hmm? What was Éclair’s full name again?”
“Lady Seyaette, correct? Understood. I will order her release immediately.”
The queen swiftly issued orders to her subordinates. Oh, she figured it out before I could even remember the name. How convenient.
“If Lady Seyaette is around, we might be able to restore some of the demi-human-friendly territories.”
“Before we go any further… why do you call me Father?”
“That’s because you are Filo-tan’s Father.”
“Huh?”
Ah, this is a difficult matter to explain. The previous Father warned me about this several times. As long as I follow the correct steps, he’ll understand.
“Let’s start by explaining about Filo-tan.”
“Uh… okay.”

I slowly began explaining my history with Father. How I acted like a fool in the first world, tormented Father, and did whatever I pleased, unaware of the country’s true nature. How I was manipulated by the Three Heroes Church, chased after Father, and ended up falling into the Pope’s trap.

And… how, when I was in the depths of despair after losing to the Spirit Tortoise and being betrayed by the pig, I was comforted by Filo-tan, the filolial raised by Father. I also mentioned how, to my eyes, what I thought were women looked like pigs, and I couldn’t understand their words. After explaining that, I told him that it would be helpful if he could interpret for me, and he agreed.
“Pigs, huh…”
“I always thought your reactions were a little strange…”
“Is that some kind of side effect of looping?”
“No, it’s not.”
“Well, whatever the reason, I get it now. …Huh? Where’s the queen?”
“She’s not a pig.”
“Wait, based on what you said, aren’t all women pigs?”
I’ll need to explain that part as well. The previous Father, Ren, and Itsuki told me exactly how to explain this, so I’ll just repeat it as they instructed.
“In other words, it’s because of Filo-tan! Anyone associated with Filo-tan is not a pig!”
Did that make sense? Well, there are a few exceptions, like the queen. Ah, just remembering it makes my heart tremble.
I want to see Filo-tan again!
“…Naofumi.”
“What?”
“Why is he looping?”
“Even if you ask me…”
“Isn’t his personality broken because of the loops?”
“Ah, that’s a classic trope in time-loop stories.”
With that, Father and the others seemed to accept it.
As expected from the previous Father and his companions!
“So, the reason he calls Naofumi Father is because the filolial raised by Naofumi… turned into a person and became a companion?”
“Since Naofumi raised her, he calls him Father…”
“So, it’s not a biological child. And filolials are those bird-shaped monsters that pull carriages, right? Like the one we had for dinner the other day? I saw them in the castle town.”
“Right. Given that Naofumi had no allies, it’s not surprising he ended up raising a monster.”
“So that’s why he calls him Father… I get it now. And there’s more to this story, isn’t there?”
“Of course. I’ll thoroughly explain the secret of my strength that Ren and Itsuki are eager to know. If I don’t tell them soon, they won’t believe me.”
At my response, Ren and Itsuki looked slightly displeased. But they didn’t seem entirely opposed to the idea.
“Sooner? What’s the reason for that?”

“Ren and Itsuki both mistakenly think this world is a game they know. That misconception becomes an obstacle to their growth. They themselves admitted in the previous loop that they were half in doubt at first.”
“A misunderstanding, huh…”
“Well, even if you say that, it’s hard to accept…”
They don’t seem to grasp it. But this reaction is expected.

“If I delay explaining, they’ll continue to believe they’ve come to a world from a game they know, and as a result, they’ll proceed with only half-baked strengthening methods, making them powerless against strong enemies.”
“Like thinking it’s a similar game, skipping the instructions, and getting stuck? You know, in games where what you learned in the first one doesn’t help in the second or third?”
Father hit the nail on the head. It was the same last time as well.

“I’ve met Ren and Itsuki countless times in previous loops where they stubbornly believed this was a game they knew and couldn’t implement the proper strengthening methods. In those cases, they called me and Father cheats and looked down on us.”
“…I can’t say I don’t understand that feeling.”
“True. Loops themselves are enough of a cheat. But if the strengthening method is wrong, there’s plenty of evidence proving it. They should believe it.”
Ren and Itsuki nodded as if they understood. It’s a relief that they’re quick to catch on.
“You’ll teach us the strengthening methods, right?”
“Of course. I’ll fully back up the leveling as well. While heroes being close to each other hinders growth… or rather, slows down level-ups, that doesn’t apply to companions.”
“A fully equipped power-leveling environment, huh… Not bad.”
“But… doesn’t that take some of the fun away?”
“Enjoying battle isn’t bad, but this is reality.”
“Yeah… after hearing those screams earlier, I get it now…”
Ah, that smoked meat sure was noisy. Seems like that’s become a bit of a trauma.
“Th-that was intense…”
“I might see that in my dreams…”
Well, they said something similar last time too. No problem.
“A-anyway, being strong isn’t a bad thing.”
“Uh… either way, we have to get stronger, right?”
The cooperation of Yuki-chan and the other filolials is essential. That’s why I want to purchase Yuki-chan and the others as soon as possible.
“So, is getting stronger the only thing we need to do after overcoming the conspiracy?”
At Ren’s question, I shake my head.
“Of course not. We also have to quickly help the people that Father and the others asked me to save.”

It’s something Father requested. Even the older sister’s older sister asked me to save as many of the village’s slaves as possible. If possible, I’d like to stop the demi-human hunts in Melromarc as well. Since the queen has returned and declared her stance, that situation should calm down somewhat.
“Someone you need to save?”
“I was asked to do many things in the previous loop.”
“Really? Then… do your best. Will you save them after getting stronger? Or will things be okay now that the queen has returned?”
“I was asked to save them as soon as possible.”
“Securing allies, huh?”
“If it can be done early, it should be a priority.”
Itsuki seems motivated, his stance showing determination.
“As for the heroes’ issues, we have to go to Faubrey, but we need to be strong enough for that first.”
Father is trying to summarize things. Ren seems ready to follow up.
“Leaving Melromarc’s problems unchecked would also be a problem, so it’s best to cooperate with the queen.”
“What about facing the waves? What are they, to begin with?”
“My memory is fuzzy on that point as well, but in the previous loop, Father and the others suspected that someone falsely claiming to be a god was involved.”
In the previous loop, I talked about the reincarnators and transmigrators who were operating behind the scenes in this world. That included the goddess from before the loop as well.
“There are people like that!? What a bunch of PKs.”
PKs, huh? He’s still thinking a bit like it’s a game.
“So, assassins are lurking around. In that case, it’s true that we need to hurry and get stronger.”
“Going to Faubrey only after becoming strong enough is also to overcome the reincarnators’ traps.”
“All I can do is protect, though…”
“The Father from the first world was very brave and led everyone. I was also guided by him. Even in the previous loop… Ren and Itsuki left all the troublesome matters to Father.”

The moment I said that, Father seemed to take a slight step back. Well, Father does tend to find things bothersome. In the first world, he often pushed the tedious stuff onto others. Even I was frequently tasked with errands on Cal Mira Island and in Faubrey.
“Repaying kindness by dumping chores on me? Well, if they trusted me, I guess it’s fine…”
“That’s a misunderstanding! I’m not lazy! There must be some reason for that!”
Ren, looking a bit put off, explained while Father’s cool facade was starting to crack.
“That’s right. In the world where Father originally lived, he managed the third-ranked guild on the server in an online game.”
“You know a lot… So, you really have been looping, huh?”
Father responded with an impressed tone.
“That’s not all. Father is someone who naturally takes care of others. It’s just that the result was him handling the tedious stuff.”
“I see…”
“We can decide on that later.”
Itsuki summarized it, then looked toward me.
“I understand the reason. I’m still a little skeptical, but it’s a story worth believing in.”
“There’s still a lot I’d like to explain, but if I cram too much information, you won’t remember it. The previous Father said that too.”

That’s why I’ve been given a list of priorities. First, I need to prove Father’s innocence and gain the trust of Ren, Itsuki, and Father. This involves resolving everything happening in Melromarc. Then, I need to raise their levels sufficiently. That includes implementing the correct strengthening methods.
“Understood. We just need to follow what Motoyasu says, right?”
“It’s settled then. So, what should we do? Based on what we just discussed, it’s about securing the allies you were asked to save in the previous loop, right?”
“That’s right. So, Father, Ren, and Itsuki, are you ready?”
“We’re only on our second day of adventuring, is this really okay? I mean… there’s this ominous feeling.”
Itsuki voiced his concern, but I puffed out my chest and nodded confidently.
“It’s fine.”
At that moment, the queen, who had been silent until now, closed her fan once and spoke up.
“Heroes, would this be a matter where we should lend our assistance?”
The queen directed the question toward me. Well then…
“Then—”
